title: Bundle alignment & scaling heuristics — cost optimizer sheet
summary: Working spreadsheet and heuristics for aligning license/support bundle choices with capacity scaling and amortization windows. Focuses on: (1) comparing on-prem purchase vs cloud VPC reserved commitments; (2) quantifying marginal cost of higher support tiers vs Ops headcount reductions; (3) rightsizing purchase lots (rack, cell, cluster) to reduce wasted headroom while preserving latency SLOs.
assumptions: All GPU capital is depreciated using straight-line amortization unless noted.
Support tiers priced as percent of annual CapEx for on-prem, and percent of committed spend for VPC.
Baseline 3-year service life for inference hardware, sensitivity tested at 2 and 5 years.
Utilization refers to token-processing capacity equivalent; spikes handled via burst pool (VPC) or spare capacity (on-prem).
Ops FTE cost is fully loaded salary + benefits, used to translate support tier delta into expected FTE reduction.
Network and datacenter colocation fees are included in Opex for on-prem scenarios where applicable.
Model quantization/packing is assumed stable across scenarios (no productivity gains baked in).
variables_definitions: GPU_unit_price: one-time purchase price per inference-optimized node (USD)
Committed_hours_price: monthly committed node-hour equivalent cost (USD)
Support_pct: annual support charge as percentage of CapEx/reserved spend
Utilization_pct: expected sustained utilization as percentage of peak capacity
Spare_ratio: fraction of extra capacity held to meet SLOs (on-prem)
Ops_FTE_cost_monthly: fully-loaded monthly cost per SRE/operator
Headroom_latency_multiplier: percent extra capacity needed to keep P95 under SLO during spikes

recommendations: Use hybrid scenario (C) as default for customers with bursty workloads and strict latency SLOs — keeps predictable low-latency footprint while minimizing upfront spend.

When support_pct differential buys >=0.6 Ops FTE in expected reduction, prefer higher support bundle; calculate break-even via Ops_FTE_cost_monthly * expected_FTE_reduction vs incremental support cost.
For customers with >75% sustained utilization, reserved VPC commitments generally win on unit economics due to higher amortized utilization and lower spare_ratio.
Right-size purchase lots to cell-level (8–12 nodes) for most customers — reduces single-event obsolescence risk and improves upgrade cadence.
Offer a formal ‘amortization fast-path’ as a sales artifact: show 2/3/5-year amortization rows to let procurement compare CapEx impact on quarterly budgets.
Include a latency-to-headroom mapping table (P95 multiplier) per workload class so sales can translate SLOs into spare_ratio recommendations; default multipliers provided in next steps.
next_steps: Build a small lookup sheet that converts P95 SLO and request-rate CV (coefficient of variation) into recommended spare_ratio; prototype with simulations from traffic traces (ask SRE for samples).
Add a checkbox in the sales quote generator that toggles amortization window and recomputes monthly equivalent cost for executive summaries.
Validate support-tier-to-FTE reduction assumptions with two customer pilots (one fintech, one media) and collect real Ops hours saved over 6 months.
Create an internal playbook one-pager mapping customer archetypes (steady, bursty, regulated) to recommended deployment mixes (On-prem, VPC, Hybrid).
Add sensitivity columns for model efficiency gains (quantization) and their impact on required node counts in 12/24 month windows.
